diagrams.title: System boundaries
diagrams.description: Local city, workers and PostgreSQL with the optional IAM-authenticated GCP judgement boundary.
diagrams.source:
...@common
direction: down
grid-columns: 2
horizontal-gap: 260
local: Local Docker environment {
  direction: down
  class: local
  operator: "Operator UI\nTrusted controller"
  world: "Synthetic city\nPhysical world engine"
  workers: "Scoped Python\nLocalAgent workers"
  db: "PostgreSQL\nDomain · queue · memory\nBudgets · audit" {shape: cylinder}
  client: "Optional CloudJudge client\nAudience-bound ID token"
  operator -> world
  operator -> workers
  world <-> db
  workers <-> db
  workers -> client: Explicit GCP judge mode
}
cloud: Optional GCP — Terraform-owned {
  direction: down
  class: cloud
  iam: "Cloud Run IAM\nCaller identity"
  gateway: "Cloud Run\nJudgement container"
  model: "Google publisher model\nVertex REST"
  image: "Artifact Registry\nImmutable image digest"
  logs: "Platform logs\nStructured gateway stdout"
  iam <-> gateway
  image -> gateway: Image {style.stroke-dash: 4}
  gateway -> model: Runtime service account ADC
  gateway -> logs
}
local <-> cloud: "Client / IAM\nHTTPS · validated verdict + usage"
(** -> **)[*].style: ${edge-style}
(** <-> **)[*].style: ${edge-style}
diagrams.reference:
flowchart TB
    subgraph Local["Local Docker environment"]
        Operator["Operator UI and trusted controller"]
        World["Synthetic city and physical world engine"]
        Workers["Scoped Python LocalAgent workers"]
        DB[("PostgreSQL: domain state, queue, memory, budgets and audit")]
        Client["Optional CloudJudge client"]
        Operator --> Workers
        Operator --> World
        World <--> DB
        Workers <--> DB
        Workers -->|"Explicit GCP judge mode"| Client
    end
    subgraph Cloud["Optional Terraform-owned GCP resources"]
        IAM["Cloud Run IAM: caller identity"]
        Gateway["Cloud Run judgement container"]
        Model["Google publisher model through Vertex REST"]
        Image["Artifact Registry: immutable image digest"]
        Logs["Platform logs and structured gateway stdout"]
        IAM --> Gateway
        Image -.-> Gateway
        Gateway -->|"Runtime service account ADC"| Model
        Gateway --> Logs
    end
    Client -->|"HTTPS and audience-bound ID token"| IAM
    Gateway -->|"Validated verdict and usage"| Client

labels: PostgreSQL Domain · queue · memory Budgets · audit
Optional CloudJudge client Audience-bound ID token
Client / IAM HTTPS · validated verdict + usage

diagrams.title: Meal handoffs
diagrams.description: Queued household, restaurant, market, dispatcher and courier handoffs with explicit substitution consent and physical arrival.
diagrams.source:
...@common
shape: sequence_diagram
household: Household agent
restaurant: Restaurant agent
market: Market agent
dispatcher: Dispatcher
courier: Courier agent
world: Physical world
household -> restaurant: household.call for pizza
restaurant -> market: market.request for missing ingredient
market.stock: Reserve own stock or forward to an unvisited market
market -> restaurant: ingredient.arrived after transfer
consent: Explicit substitution consent {
  restaurant -> household: Offer replacement
  household -> restaurant: Explicit approval required
}
restaurant.stock: Cook only from arrived, reserved ingredients
restaurant -> dispatcher: basket.ready
dispatcher -> courier: courier.briefed
courier -> dispatcher: courier.accepted
world -> dispatcher: delivery.arrived after road traversal
dispatcher -> dispatcher: dispatch.complete records delivered status
household -> household: meal.delivery checks canonical job status
(** -> **)[*].style: ${edge-style}
diagrams.reference:
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Household agent
    participant R as Restaurant agent
    participant M as Market agent
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant C as Courier agent
    participant W as Physical world
    H->>R: household.call for pizza
    R->>M: market.request for missing ingredient
    Note over M: Reserve own stock or forward to an unvisited market
    M->>R: ingredient.arrived after transfer
    Note over H,R: A replacement requires explicit household approval
    Note over R: Cook only from arrived, reserved ingredients
    R->>D: basket.ready
    D->>C: courier.briefed
    C->>D: courier.accepted
    W->>D: delivery.arrived after road traversal
    D->>D: dispatch.complete records delivered status
    H->>H: meal.delivery checks canonical job status

labels: Reserve own stock or forward to an unvisited market
Cook only from arrived, reserved ingredients

diagrams.title: An agent's transaction
diagrams.description: A committed attempt reservation precedes the atomic transaction for tool effects, memory, outgoing events and ACK.
diagrams.reference:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Trusted controller
    participant A as Scoped LocalAgent
    participant Q as PostgreSQL queue
    participant T as Domain tools and memory
    C->>Q: Publish an addressed event
    A->>Q: Claim with role subscriptions
    Q-->>A: Event, attempt and fenced lease token
    A->>Q: Reserve attempt and full tool allowance
    Note over A,Q: Reservation commits before handling
    A->>Q: Begin effects transaction and validate lease
    A->>T: Read authoritative facts and current-context memory
    A->>T: Execute allowed actions and append memory revisions
    A->>Q: Record decision and publish outgoing events
    A->>Q: ACK in the same transaction
    Note over Q,T: Commit together, or roll back together

labels: Effects transaction — commit or roll back together

diagrams.title: Restaurant supply and consent
diagrams.description: Ingredient sourcing and shortage forwarding return to the restaurant; substitutions require household approval.
diagrams.source:
...@common
shape: sequence_diagram
household: Household
restaurant: Restaurant
market: Nearest market
other: Another market
delivery: Dispatcher + courier
household -> restaurant: Queued meal call
restaurant -> market: Ingredient request
market -> other: Shortage forwarding
stock: Reserved stock transfers from the eligible source {
  market -> restaurant: Reserved, then arrived
  other -> restaurant: Reserved, then arrived if forwarded
}
consent: Explicit substitution consent {
  restaurant -> household: Substitution offer
  household -> restaurant: Explicit approval
}
restaurant -> delivery: Cook from arrived stock
delivery -> household: Confirmed delivery
(** -> **)[*].style: ${edge-style}
diagrams.reference:
flowchart LR
    H[Household] -->|queued meal call| R[Restaurant]
    R -->|ingredient request| M[Nearest market]
    M -->|shortage forwarding| N[Another market]
    M -->|reserved then arrived| R
    N -->|reserved then arrived| R
    R -->|substitution offer| H
    H -->|explicit approval| R
    R -->|cook from arrived stock| D[Dispatcher and courier]
    D -->|confirmed delivery| H

labels: Reserved stock transfers from the eligible source

diagrams.title: Delivery queue lineage
diagrams.description: Inventory, fulfillment, dispatch and physical world events pass through the PostgreSQL queue.
diagrams.source:
...@common
shape: sequence_diagram
scenario: Scenario
queue: Postgres queue {class: durable}
inventory: Inventory / own store
fulfillment: Fulfillment / own store
dispatcher: Dispatcher / run fleet
world: Trusted physical world
scenario -> queue: basket.requested
queue -> inventory: Inventory handles the addressed event
inventory -> queue: basket.reserved
queue -> fulfillment: Fulfillment handles the addressed event
fulfillment -> queue: basket.ready
queue -> dispatcher: Dispatcher handles the addressed event
dispatcher -> queue: delivery.assigned
world -> queue: delivery.arrived
dispatcher -> queue: delivery.completed
(** -> **)[*].style: ${edge-style}
diagrams.reference:
flowchart LR
    S[Scenario] -->|basket.requested| Q[(Postgres queue)]
    Q --> I[Inventory: own store]
    I -->|basket.reserved| Q
    Q --> F[Fulfillment: own store]
    F -->|basket.ready| Q
    Q --> D[Dispatcher: run fleet]
    D -->|delivery.assigned| Q
    W[Trusted physical world] -->|delivery.arrived| Q
    D -->|delivery.completed| Q

diagrams.title: Durable inference lifecycle
diagrams.description: Short transactions persist request, dispatch and result around provider I/O. Fresh validation commits an approved or denied receipt, memory, outbox and ACK atomically; an uncertain dispatch is never automatically resent.
diagrams.reference:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Scoped judge worker
    participant D as PostgreSQL
    participant P as Bounded provider
    A->>D: Prepare immutable request under fenced lease
    D-->>A: Commit request, context and local proposal
    A->>D: Commit dispatch marker and call allowance
    Note over A,D: Close connection before remote I/O
    A->>P: Invoke with sanitized numeric facts
    P-->>A: Schema-validated verdict
    A->>D: Save result in a short fenced transaction
    D-->>A: Commit saved result
    A->>D: Re-read current state and validate saved proposal
    Note over A,D: Apply effects, memory, outbox and ACK atomically
    D-->>A: Commit completed event

labels: PREPARED Immutable request + proposal Precondition hash committed
IN_FLIGHT Dispatch marker + one-call budget Committed before provider I/O
Provider I/O No database connection held
SUCCEEDED Validated result saved Short transaction
UNKNOWN / FAIL CLOSED Never resend automatically Apply a denied review
Fresh Queue.process transaction Recheck saved result, facts Deadline + candidate
DENIED / NO RETRY Stale, unknown or refused No reassignment
APPLIED Approved OR denied receipt Effects + memory + outbox + ACK One atomic transaction
Saved result or unknown Reuse result without a new call
